title: Introduction to Computer Programming for the Physical Sciences
description: An introduction to programming and data analysis for the physical sciences. Topics include syntax, goodcoding practice, basic algorithmic structure, plotting, basic data analysis, numerical root-finding and integration.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 2B or 3B or Physics 8 or AP Calculus BC Exam with a score of 5

title: Readings in Physics
description: Critical reviews and discussions of selected physics subjects, conducted under the supervision of a Physics faculty member.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of instructor.

title: Introduction to Physics Research
description: Independent research conducted under the guidance of a Physics faculty member. Topic and scope varies, to be specified by student and supervisory faculty member prior to registration.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of instructor.

title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
description: Linear Algebra: Vector spaces, operators, spectral decomposition. Topics may include Sturm-Liouville equations, special functions. Fourier series and Fourier transforms, Dirac delta-function.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better.

title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
description: Analytic functions, contour integrals and branch cuts. Conformal mapping. Laplace transforms. Asymptotic series and the gamma function. Greens functions.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 5C or 6B with a grade of C- or better.

title: Intermediate Mechanics and Special Relativity
description: Newtonian mechanics in 3D. Conservation laws. Complex numbers. Oscillations. Inertial reference frames, Lorentz transformations, relativistic momentum and energy, four-vectors.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 2 or 22 with a minimum grade of C-. Mathematics 6A (may be taken concurrently)

title: Advanced Mechanics
description: Calculus of variations. Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics. Central force problems and collision theory. Non-inertial reference frames. Coupled oscillations and waves.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 103 with a grade of C- or better.

title: Nonlinear Phenomena
description: An introduction to nonlinear phenomena. Flows and bifurcations in one and two dimensions, chaos, fractals, strange attractors. Applications to physics, engineering, chemistry, and biology.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 105A or Physics 103; or ME 163 or upper-division standing in ECE.

title: Electromagnetism
description: Electrostatics, Laplace's equation, method of images, separation of variables, multipole expansion, magnetostatics, electric and magnetic fields in matter.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 5 or 25 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 6B with minimum grade of C-.

title: Electromagnetism
description: Electrodynamics, Maxwells equations, conservation laws, electromagnetic waves, potentials and fields for moving charges, radiation, special relativity.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 110A with a minimum grade of C-.

title: Quantum Mechanics
description: The postulates of quantum mechanics, the Schrdinger equation and its consequences, the quantum harmonic oscillator and other one dimensional quantum systems, Hilbert Space and Dirac notation, the hydrogen atom.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 5 or 25 and Physics 100A with a minimum grade of C-.

title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Spin and angular momentum, Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, identical particles, symmetries and conservation laws, time independent perturbation theory.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 115A with a minimum grade of C-.

title: Quantum Mechanics
description: The variational principle, time dependent perturbation theory, the adiabatic theorem. Topics from: WKB approximation, the Dirac equation, Berrys phase, Bells inequality, quantum cryptography, quantum computation.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 115B with a minimum grade of C-.

title: Group Theory for Physicists
description: The emphasis is on developing some intuition about the role of symmetries in physics, rather than going through rigorous mathematical proofs. Theorems will be proved at the level of rigor customary among physicists.
prerequisites_raw: Physics PHYS 110A

title: Thermal and Statistical Physics
description: Principles of statistical physics, entropy, large numbers, thermodynamic principles, microcanonical ensemble, ideal gas, free energy, chemical potential, selected applications. Canonical ensemble, if time permits.
prerequisites_raw: PHYS 22 and MATH 6B with a minimum grade of C-

title: Thermal and Statistical Physics
description: Canonical ensemble and partition functions, grand canonical ensemble, quantum statistics, Fermi-Dirac, Bose-Einstein distribution laws. Topics from: Brownian motion, Langevin equation, dissipation and fluctuations, elementary kinetic theory, weakly interacting gases or mean field theory of magnetism, other topics illustrative of the breadth of the subject and/or selected applications.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 115A and Physics 119A with a minimum grade of C-.

title: Physics of California Waves, Weather, Quakes and Fires
description: Why do the waves hit the beach every five seconds? This course teaches students the relevant fluid dynamics and allows them to apply it to natural phenomena of California: seismic waves, tsunamis, maximum tree heights, fluid flow around fish.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 5 or 25.

title: Condensed Matter Physics
description: Classification of solids; crystal symmetry; thermal, electronic, and magnetic properties of metals, semiconductors, and insulators; band theory of electronic states; wave scattering by crystals; semiconductor devices.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 115A with at least a C- or better, and upper-division standing.

title: Condensed Matter Physics
description: Tight binding model, topological insulator, magnetism, phase transition, introduction to superconductivity.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 115B with a minimum grade of C-.

title: Elementary Particle Physics
description: Introduction to quarks and leptons and the phenomenology of the particles they comprise; fundamental symmetries, invariance principles, and the associated quantum numbers, strong, electromagnetic, and weak interactions and their relationship.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 115B.

title: Laboratory Optics
description: An introduction to optical phenomena and the methods and instrumentation used to generate, measure, and manipulate light. Experiments will cover imaging and aberrations, coherence, diffraction, interference, interferometry, Fourier optics, reflection and polarization, spectroscopy, lasers, fiber optics, and optical instruments.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 141 with a grade of C- or better, Physics 29 with a grade of C- or better, and Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better.

title: Analog Electronics
description: Passive circuits, diodes, transistors, field effect transistors, operational amplifiers, feedback and control. Design, building and testing of analog circuits.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 13CL or 20CL and Math 3B with a minimum grade of C-.

title: Digital Electronics
description: Gates, combinational and sequential logic, ?multiplexers, counters, shift registers, memory and microprocessors. Design, building and testing of digital circuitry, including a modern microprocessor based computer system.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 127AL with a minimum grade of C-.

title: Advanced Experimental Physics
description: Selected experiments in physics, i.e. saturated absorption spectroscopy, muon lifetime measurements, pulsed nuclear magnetic resonance, Mossbauer effect. Develop skills in detailing observations in a scientific notebook, data collection and error analysis, operating complex physical apparatus, and scientific communication.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 13CL or Physics 20CL or Physics CS 15C. Physics 115A (may be taken concurrently).

title: Introduction to Scientific Computation
description: A survey of computers, programming, and computational techniques for the natural sciences. Physical foundations of computation, binary arithmetic, computer architecture, programming languages, operating systems, UNIX shell and filesystems. Programming tools, variables and data structures, expressions, control flow, files, functions and scoping, objects, error handling, debugging, graphics, text processing, networking, data acquisition and transfer. Mathematics and algorithms for data processing and analysis, numerical methods, random numbers and simulation.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 5 or 25 with a grade of C- or better, and Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better; Physics 29 with a grade of C- or better.

title: Gravitation and Relativity
description: An introduction to Einstein's general relativity, the spacetime of special relativity, the principle of equivalence, gravity as geometry, the description of spacetime geometry, the spacetime of a relativistic star, solar system test of general relativity, gravitational collapse, black holes, cosmology.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 103-104 with a minimum grade of C- in each.
